symptom: describe of a navigation list item with a CSS class printed `item (Action: …, ButtonStyle: nav-orders)` — not an item property, and unparseable unquoted (`nav-orders` reads as a subtraction: "extraneous input '{' expecting {',', ')'}") — and CREATE wrote an empty Forms$Appearance whatever the item said, so a styled item lost its class on describe → exec
cause: parseNavigationListItems copied Appearance.Class into rawWidget.ButtonStyle and the navigationlist emitter printed it as ButtonStyle; pages.NavigationListItem had no appearance fields, so buildNavigationListItemV3 had nowhere to put Class/Style and navListItemToGen hard-coded newAppearance("", "", "", nil)
insight: An item is not a pages.Widget, so applyWidgetAppearance never reached it and every appearance property had to be threaded by hand — check that path first whenever a non-widget child (item, tab page, template) loses a property. Every Studio Pro item measured (PedApp Grid_WithNavigation, WidgetDemo_Showcase) stores the same Forms$Appearance as a widget (Class, DesignProperties, DynamicClasses, Style), so no new shape was needed. The control that settles it is a describe → exec round trip on a styled item: the pre-fix describe did not even parse, the fixed one re-executes as "Unchanged". Design properties on an item are still not printed or written (theme key for NavigationListItem unmeasured).
